title: Exam Mix 01 — Core Concepts
description: Mixed revision: relational rules, ER modelling and keys, normalisation, and SQL.

items.question: The Week 2 library permits at most five books on loan per member. A member currently has five and returns one. A different book has available copies. What does the borrowing limit permit?

options.text: No new loan until all books are returned
One new loan before reaching the limit again
Two new loans
No loan because the limit counts returned books

items.explanation: Four books remain on loan after the return. One more is allowed because the limit applies to books borrowed at the same time.

references.label: Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer, p. 13

items.question: In the bookstore ERD, each order item refers to one order and one book. Which pair of references belongs in ORDER_ITEMS?

options.text: User_ID and Author_ID
Book_ID and Author_ID
Order_ID and Book_ID
Order_ID and User_ID

items.explanation: The two references connect the order item to the order it belongs to and the book it records.

items.question: SPORT contains sport numbers 1 and 2. STUDENT_ENROLL contains (SID 10, sportNO 1) and (SID 11, sportNO NULL). What does a FULL OUTER JOIN on sportNO return?

options.text: Only the match for sport 1
The match and SID 11 only
The match and sport 2 only
The match, SID 11 without a sport, and sport 2 without a student

items.explanation: A full outer join includes the match and both unmatched rows, filling missing columns with NULL.

items.question: The Week 4 example records Biology 2 only in Susan Johnson’s student row. Which design lets the school delete Susan’s record without losing Biology 2?

options.text: Store classes separately and link students to classes
Sort the combined table by class
Rename the class before deleting Susan
Store the class twice in Susan’s row

items.explanation: Keeping classes independently means removing a student does not remove the only record of the class.

items.question: A travel booking already has a payment transaction. The agency requires exactly one associated payment transaction per booking. Which action violates this rule?

options.text: Keeping the existing payment
Adding a second payment while keeping the first
Looking up the linked payment
Correcting a detail on the existing payment

items.explanation: A second associated transaction would give the booking two payments.

items.question: A child entity cannot exist without its parent, and its primary key includes the parent’s key. How does the Week 3 lecture classify the child?

options.text: Strong entity
Derived attribute
Weak entity
Alternate key

items.explanation: The weak entity is existence-dependent and its key is partly or wholly derived from its parent.

items.question: A 1NF inventory table has primary key (Player_Id, Item) and only one non-key attribute, Quantity. Quantity requires both key columns. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: Quantity is a repeating group
Item alone is the primary key
Quantity has a partial dependency
The table meets the 2NF requirement

items.explanation: The non-key attribute depends on the entire key, so there is no partial dependency.

items.question: In FROM club c, what does c mean in WHERE c.clubname = 'pool'?

options.text: An alias for the club table
A new database table
An alias for the literal pool
A second filter condition

items.explanation: The alias c is a short name for club within the query and qualifies clubname.

items.question: The Mini Library allows each physical copy to have only one active loan at a time. Copy C01 is on loan, and its ReturnDate is empty because it has not been returned. Can another member borrow that same physical copy now?

options.text: Yes, because the borrower is different
No, because C01 already has an active loan
Yes, because the title may have other copies
No, because a physical copy can only be borrowed once

items.explanation: C01 has not been returned, so its loan is still active. The limit applies to the physical copy, regardless of who wants to borrow it. Another copy of the same title might be available, but C01 cannot be lent again until it is returned.

items.question: A design is already in 2NF. A non-key column B determines another non-key column C, and the primary key A determines B. What change follows the 3NF conversion shown in the lecture?

options.text: Repeat C in more rows
Make A and C a repeating group
Store C with its determinant B in a separate table and retain B as the link
Remove B and C without preserving their values

items.explanation: The dependency A → B → C is indirect. Moving C with B keeps the fact with its determinant.
